name: Patient Intake Triage Protocol Knowledge Base
disclaimer: This protocol knowledge base is strictly for intake routing and urgency prioritization. It does not provide medical diagnoses. Uncertain or high-risk cases must immediately escalate to a qualified clinician.

urgency_levels.name: Immediate (Resuscitation)
urgency_levels.description: Life or limb-threatening conditions requiring instantaneous medical intervention.

urgency_levels.name: Emergent
urgency_levels.description: High risk of rapid deterioration or severe distress requiring rapid provider evaluation.

urgency_levels.name: Urgent
urgency_levels.description: Serious condition requiring multiple diagnostic resources, patient hemodynamically stable.

urgency_levels.name: Less Urgent
urgency_levels.description: Stable condition requiring single diagnostic test or minor therapeutic intervention.

urgency_levels.name: Non-Urgent
urgency_levels.description: Routine complaints requiring minimal resources or symptomatic reassurance.

rules.title: Suspected Acute Coronary Syndrome / High-Risk Chest Pain
triggers: chest pain with diaphoresis (sweating)
chest pressure radiating to left arm, neck, or jaw
crushing or squeezing substernal tightness with shortness of breath
chest discomfort with dizziness, near-syncope, or cold clammy skin
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-CHEST-01: Chest pain or pressure accompanied by autonomic symptoms (diaphoresis, nausea), pain radiation to upper extremity/jaw, or respiratory distress carries high suspicion of Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) and requires immediate Resuscitation Bay routing and immediate human clinical assessment without diagnostic delay.

rules.title: Acute Pleuritic or Positional Chest Pain
triggers: sharp chest pain worsened by deep inspiration or coughing
sudden onset unilateral pleuritic pain without trauma
chest pain with unexplained tachycardia or calf swelling
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-CHEST-02: Acute sharp pleuritic chest discomfort warrants urgent rule-out for pulmonary thromboembolism, spontaneous pneumothorax, or acute pericarditis. Requires 12-lead ECG and immediate physician evaluation.

rules.title: Subacute Musculoskeletal / Reproducible Chest Wall Pain
triggers: pain precisely reproducible by pressing on specific costochondral joint
ache following heavy lifting or exercise without shortness of breath or sweating
gradual onset superficial chest wall tenderness
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-CHEST-03: Localized chest pain strictly reproducible by direct chest wall palpation with negative cardiovascular screens (no radiation, no diaphoresis, no dyspnea) is suitable for Urgent Care evaluation.

rules.title: Critical Airway Compromise or Respiratory Failure
triggers: stridor or severe audible wheezing with tripoding posture
cyanosis of lips, tongue, or fingertips
inability to complete single-word sentences due to breathlessness
altered mental status, extreme agitation, or severe lethargy from hypoxia
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-BREATH-01: Inability to speak in full sentences, cyanosis, audible stridor, or severe work of breathing indicates impending respiratory failure. Requires immediate code/resuscitation allocation and airway team standby.

rules.title: Acute Bronchospasm or Moderate Respiratory Distress
triggers: acute asthma or COPD exacerbation unresponsive to home inhaler
shortness of breath with fever and productive rust-colored sputum
breathing difficulty with known congestive heart failure and orthopnea
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-BREATH-02: Acute bronchospasm unresponsive to rescue bronchodilators or dyspnea complicated by underlying cardiopulmonary history warrants emergent ED assessment and nebulized therapy.

rules.title: Mild Respiratory Tract Infection without Distress
triggers: mild shortness of breath with nasal congestion and sore throat
able to speak in uninterrupted paragraphs
chronic mild smoker cough without acute change or distress
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-BREATH-03: Mild upper respiratory symptoms with normal conversational capability, no resting tachypnea, and no accessory muscle utilization routed to Fast Track.

rules.title: Neonatal / High-Risk Meningeal or Septic Fever Screen
triggers: fever >= 38.0C (100.4F) in infant under 3 months of age
fever accompanied by neck stiffness, photophobia, or confusion
fever with non-blanching petechial or purpuric skin rash
immunocompromised patient (chemotherapy, transplant) with fever >= 38.3C
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-FEVER-01: Fever in neonates (<90 days) or fever combined with meningeal signs (stiff neck, photophobia) or non-blanching rash requires immediate emergent routing for sepsis/meningitis workup and direct physician escalation.

rules.title: Fever with Significant Dehydration or Intractable Vomiting
triggers: persistent high fever (>39C) lasting >72 hours
fever with inability to keep liquids down for >12 hours
fever with postural dizziness or marked lethargy
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-FEVER-02: Prolonged fever with signs of systemic dehydration or inability to maintain oral hydration warrants Urgent care for intravenous fluid rehydration and lab investigation.

rules.title: Uncomplicated Acute Viral Syndrome / Mild Fever
triggers: fever < 38.8C for 1-2 days with common cold or mild malaise
alert adult patient tolerating oral fluids normally
mild fever without focal neurological, respiratory, or abdominal red flags
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-FEVER-03: Mild-to-moderate fever of short duration (<3 days) in an alert, well-hydrated adult with no high-risk comorbidities or focal signs routes to Walk-In Ambulatory Clinic.

rules.title: Major Trauma / Neurovascular Compromise / High Kinetic Mechanism
triggers: penetrating injury to head, neck, torso, or groin
severe deformity of limb with cold/pulseless distal extremity
fall > 3 meters or high-speed vehicular rollover with loss of consciousness
active uncontrollable arterial hemorrhage
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-INJURY-01: High-energy kinetic mechanism, penetrative trauma, pulseless injured extremity, or uncontrolled bleeding triggers Level 1 Resuscitation and immediate trauma team activation.

rules.title: Suspected Fracture / Significant Blunt Extremity Trauma
triggers: twisted ankle or knee with immediate inability to take 4 weight-bearing steps
fall onto outstretched hand with focal wrist tenderness or visible bump
deep laceration requiring sutures with controlled bleeding
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-INJURY-02: Isolated extremity trauma with positive weight-bearing deficit or bony focal tenderness (Ottawa rules positive) requires radiographic imaging and orthopedic evaluation.

rules.title: Minor Contusion, Superficial Abrasion, or Mild Strain
triggers: minor scrape or bruise with intact skin and minimal swelling
mild muscle strain occurring >24 hours ago, able to walk and move normally
superficial papercut or minor skin scratch with no infection
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-INJURY-03: Low-velocity superficial soft tissue trauma with full mobility and preserved neurovascular integrity routes to Walk-In Ambulatory Clinic.

rules.title: Acute Surgical Abdomen / Peritoneal Shock Screen
triggers: sudden catastrophic abdominal pain with rigid board-like abdomen
severe abdominal pain with syncope, profound dizziness, or hypotension
acute severe lower pelvic pain in female of childbearing age with missed period
vomiting blood (hematemesis) or black tarry stools (melena)
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-ABDOM-01: Acute severe abdomen presenting with involuntary rigidity, hemodynamic collapse, active GI hemorrhage, or suspected ruptured ectopic pregnancy triggers immediate emergency surgical evaluation.

rules.title: Focal Acute Abdominal Pain (Appendicitis / Cholecystitis Screen)
triggers: pain starting around navel then migrating to right lower abdomen with nausea
sharp right upper quadrant pain after eating fatty food, radiating to shoulder
severe flank pain radiating to groin in colicky waves
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-ABDOM-02: Progressive focal abdominal pain with migration to RLQ or RUQ warrants urgent diagnostic laboratory and ultrasound/CT imaging for acute appendicitis, cholecystitis, or nephrolithiasis.

rules.title: Mild Acute Gastroenteritis / Dyspepsia
triggers: diffuse crampy belly discomfort with mild loose stools and no blood
mild burning indigestion after meals with soft non-tender abdomen
nausea without dehydration, tolerating oral fluids
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-ABDOM-03: Mild crampy abdominal discomfort without focal tenderness, peritoneal signs, or bloody stool is appropriate for outpatient or urgent care symptomatic management.

rules.title: Clinical Escalation for Incomplete, Ambiguous, or High-Risk Presentations
triggers: patient presentation contains critical ambiguities or unexplained vital instability
symptoms cannot be safely categorized by standard outpatient rules
unconscious, severely confused, or medically unstable patient
rules.citation_text: Protocol R-ESCALATE-01: The triage system identified critical informational gaps or elevated risk indicators that cannot be safely reconciled by outpatient heuristic rules. Mandated immediate bedside triage nurse or physician evaluation.
